verdict.rationale: Aider's git integration auto-commits and lets users review and `/undo` the AI's code edits. That versions the outputs of AI runs, not the automations themselves. Aider has no documented automation entity, such as a saved script, scheduled job or workflow definition, with its own versioning, review or rollback. Scripting via `--message` or the Python `Coder` API and `.aider.conf.yml` are building blocks; versioning them would be the user's own git workaround.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations
